title: A generic closed subset has fibrewise thin closure in a smooth trait scheme
statement: Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], $F=\operatorname{Frac}R$ its localization at all nonzero elements, $k=R/\mathfrak m_R$, and $T=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $Y\to T$ be a smooth separated morphism of finite type [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]; separated means that its diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Write $Y_F$ and $Y_k$ for its generic and closed fibres [def-pc-base-change]. Let $Z_F\hookrightarrow Y_F$ be a closed subscheme whose underlying closed subset contains no irreducible component of $Y_F$ [def-weil-irreducible-components]. Let $Z\hookrightarrow Y$ be its scheme-theoretic closure, meaning the scheme-theoretic image of $Z_F\to Y_F\to Y$ [def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-image]. The open subscheme $Y\setminus |Z|$ [def-weil-open-immersion] has generic fibre $Y_F\setminus |Z_F|$ and is dense in every geometric fibre of $Y\to T$: for each point $t\in T$ and each algebraically closed extension $\Omega/\kappa(t)$, its pullback is dense in $Y\times_T\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$. In particular $|Z|$ contains no irreducible component of $Y_k$. Empty fibres and $Z_F=\varnothing$ are allowed.

proof.text: Choose a uniformizer $\pi\in R$. Apply smooth-trait infrastructure to $Y$: it is Noetherian and regular, the generic fibre is a quasi-compact open, the special fibre is reduced, and at every special-fibre component generic point $\xi$ the ring $\mathcal O_{Y,\xi}$ is a DVR with uniformizer $\pi$. Regularity and the normal-component decomposition imply that each point of $Y$ has an affine neighbourhood inside a single integral open-and-closed component. We will use these conclusions without any purity-of-relative-dimension assumption.

source.place: BLR 6.5 Theorem 1 proof, printed p.162 (PDF p.168), thin-closure assertion; existing smooth-trait infrastructure and normal decomposition supply the local geometry.

proof.text:
For any affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subset Y$, the affine generic-fibre model identifies $U_F$ with $\operatorname{Spec}A[1/\pi]$. Write $Z_F\cap U_F=\operatorname{Spec}(A[1/\pi]/J)$ using the affine description of a closed immersion. Thus $g:Z_F\to Y$ has affine inverse image over every affine open and is affine, hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated. The quasi-compact scheme-image kernel theorem identifies the ideal of $Z\cap U$ with
$$I=\ker(A\longrightarrow A[1/\pi]/J)=\{a\in A:a/1\in J\}.$$
It follows directly that $\pi^na\in I$ implies $a\in I$, since $\pi$ is a unit in the target ring. Also $IA[1/\pi]=J$: for $a/\pi^n\in J$, its numerator $a/1$ lies in $J$, so $a\in I$; the reverse inclusion follows from the definition of $I$.

source.place: Tags 01R8 (lemma-quasi-compact-scheme-theoretic-image), 01S7 (lemma-affine-separated); affine principal-open generic-fibre model and the displayed elementary contraction calculation.

proof.text: Restrict the scheme-theoretic image of $g$ to the open $Y_F$. The open restriction theorem applies because $g$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, as just proved. The restricted morphism is the closed immersion $Z_F\hookrightarrow Y_F$, whose scheme-theoretic image is its source. Consequently $Z\times_Y Y_F=Z_F$ as closed subschemes, and the open complement $V=Y\setminus|Z|$ has generic fibre $Y_F\setminus|Z_F|$.

source.place: Tag 01R8, lemma-quasi-compact-scheme-theoretic-image, restriction to opens; a closed immersion is its own image.

proof.text: Fix a generic point $\xi$ of a nonempty special-fibre component. Choose an affine neighbourhood $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ inside its integral open-and-closed ambient component $C$, using the decomposition of step 1; thus $A$ is a domain. Let $\mathfrak p\subset A$ represent $\xi$. The affine stalk theorem gives $A_{\mathfrak p}\cong\mathcal O_{Y,\xi}$, compatibly with germs, so the image of $\pi$ in $A$ is nonzero (its image in that DVR is a uniformizer). Thus $U_F$ is nonempty. The open $C_F\subset C$ is nonempty and irreducible, and is open-and-closed in $Y_F$, so it is an irreducible component of $Y_F$. The nonempty open $U_F$ is dense in $C_F$. If the ideal $J$ of step 2 were zero, the closed subset $|Z_F|$ would contain $U_F$ and hence $C_F$, contrary to the hypothesis. Therefore $J\ne0$.

The ring $B\cong\mathcal O_{Y,\xi}$ is the DVR of step 1 with uniformizer $\pi$. Choose $0
e b\in IB$. By the unit-times-uniformizer-power theorem, $b=u\pi^m$ for a unit $u\in B$. Multiplying by $u^{-1}$ gives $\pi^m\in IB$, and the saturation proved in step 5 gives $1\in IB$. Hence $IB=B$. This means $I

source.place: Tag 00PD, lemma-characterize-dvr, final assertion; apply it to the DVR stalk, then use saturation.

proof.text: Every component of either ordinary fibre has a generic point, by sobriety of schemes. In the generic fibre the hypothesis and step 3 put each such generic point in $V_F$; in the special fibre step 6 puts each in $V_k$. For each component $D$ with generic point $\eta_D$, the closure of $V_t$ contains $\overline{\{\eta_D\}}=D$. Components cover the fibre, so $V_t$ is dense for both points $t\in T$. There are exactly these two points because $R$ is a DVR: every nonzero prime contains a nonzero element $u\pi^m$, hence contains $\pi$ and is the maximal ideal. Empty fibres have empty underlying space and satisfy the same density conclusion vacuously.

proof.text: Apply smooth fibrewise-density base change to the open immersion $V\hookrightarrow Y$: smoothness is assumed and density in every ordinary fibre was established in step 7. For $t\in T$ and an algebraically closed extension $\Omega/\kappa(t)$, take $T'=\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to T$. Its unique fibre is $Y\times_T\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, so the cited theorem gives the required density there. If $Z_F$ is empty, its affine ideals $J$ are unit ideals, whence the contractions $I$ are unit ideals as well; thus $Z$ is empty and $V=Y$. Empty $Y$ is covered by the same argument. No perfection, completeness, or excellence assumption on $R$ has been used.

BLR is not in the local literature (the report lists it as WANTED), so I checked the agent's proof directly against the cited statements. The delivery adds no new nodes and leaves the statement and stmt_deps unchanged. Steps: (1) The smooth-trait infrastructure node gives Noetherian, regular, reduced Y_k and DVR stalks with uniformizer pi; regular-normal (1),(2) gives integral clopen components. (2) The generic-fibre ring-model node needs a reduced closed fibre, which step 1 supplies. Affine permanence makes U_F affine and g affine, hence qc. The qc-kernel node gives I=ker(A->A[1/pi]/J). I checked saturation and I*A[1/pi]=J. (3) Image restricted to the open Y_F plus image of a closed immersion gives Z x_Y Y_F = Z_F, so V_F = Y_F\|Z_F|. (4) A is a domain and pi is nonzero through the stalk localization (c). C_F is clopen and irreducible, so it is a component of Y_F. J=0 would contradict the hypothesis. (5) Elementary; the denominator t is written out explicitly. (6) The unit-times-pi^m node gives 1 in IB, so I is not in p and xi is not in Z. (7) Sobriety and components-cover give density in both fibres, and T has exactly two points. (8) The fibrewise-density base change with T'=Spec Omega gives the geometric-fibre clause. Edge cases checked: Y empty, Y_k empty, Z_F empty, A^1_R with V(x) and V(pi x-1), mixed relative dimensions, nonreduced Z_F.
